## Research

### Analog Circuit Engineering (ACE) Lab {#ace-lab}

[Harvey Mudd College, Department of Engineering | March 2026 - Present |
Advisor: Prof. Matthew Spencer]{.entry-meta}

The ACE Lab is building a compact, low-power, research-grade
electropenetrograph (EPG) sensor for research on insect feeding behavior. The
team is split into analog, firmware, and software subteams. I am on the
firmware team, where I write and debug C firmware for the version of the
sensor built on a Nordic nRF development kit, primarily resolving
communication issues between the analog front end and the host software.

My current work covers:

- Stabilizing the Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) link to a custom host
  application over the Nordic UART Service, and posting control-loop state and
  compressed waveform data back to the host.
- Replacing an external signal-generator chip with direct digital synthesis
  (DDS) in firmware.
- Adding configurable time-averaged (chopped) input-resistance (Ri)
  measurement.
- Characterizing and reducing the sensor's power consumption, with a target
  reduction of over 90%.

**Skills:** C, Zephyr RTOS, nRF Connect SDK, BLE (Nordic UART Service),
direct digital synthesis

### Sustainability and Network Design (SAND) Lab {#sand-lab}

[Harvey Mudd College, Department of Computer Science | May 2026 - Present |
Advisor: Prof. Arthi Padmanabhan]{.entry-meta}

This project measures the energy consumption and carbon-equivalent emissions
that LLM crawlers and other bot traffic add to a web server. Over 700,000
requests from historical server logs are classified by source, such as
crawlers, scrapers, cloud providers, and residential users, and replayed
against a Raspberry Pi web server running Apache with TWiki and WordPress
while a USB power meter records its power draw. Scheduled replays are then
compared against grid carbon-intensity data to estimate how shifting traffic
in time changes emissions. I write Python and Bash tooling on Linux for the
measurement and analysis pipeline. A paper on the results is in preparation.

**Skills:** Python, Bash, Linux, Raspberry Pi, Apache, power measurement,
carbon-intensity analysis
